answer: A trust-graph protocol mitigates Sybil attacks by evaluating bottleneck cuts in transaction topologies. To gain influence, an adversary incurs the verifiable cost of transacting with established nodes to acquire scarce trust edges. Any localized reputation delta cannot easily ripple across honest partitions, preventing malicious clusters from creating an unmonitored haven. However, this design inherently marginalizes newly initialized agents lacking established counterparty histories.
